working_title: Rainfall pulses increase frog active-community richness through species-selective reassembly
central_claims: Within matched route × seasonal-window comparisons, wetter runs contain more acoustically active species, and richness gain increases with rainfall contrast.
Rainfall-associated richness gain is not explained by simple nested addition; exact consecutive-year comparisons show increased compositional turnover with rainfall contrast.
Species wet-versus-dry responses are strongly heterogeneous and remain so after pair-level temperature, survey-date, rain-contrast magnitude and year-gap adjustment.
The species-selective pattern is the central ecological result; it rejects a uniform activation response by an unchanged assemblage.
secondary_results: Pooled species responses are negatively associated with body size in AmphiBIO.
The body-size association does not survive family-stratified permutation (two-sided P=0.314), so body size is not authorized as the headline mechanism.
Earlier participation/residual-association decomposition supports membership-level change more than pairwise co-calling change.
interpretation: Short rainfall pulses are associated with transient, species-selective reassembly of the acoustically active frog assemblage.
prohibited: classical environmental filtering through species establishment or persistence
body size is a proven rainfall-filtering mechanism
body-size gradient is phylogenetically or family robust
temporary-water breeding strategy or hydroperiod is directly tested
FrogID directly replicates the matched NAAMP community-reassembly result
